This page implements [`6_locate_clinics.R`][legacy-6] at pinned revision
`31e0769683e133e136b09ac0c6608c5a12657a9a`. Each row is a clinic-location
candidate, not necessarily a unique clinic. Matching ties and full-join-only
clinics remain visible. Five reported coordinate sources, a matched FKT,
and a healthshed supply the evidence for the fixed source-selection order.
A selected centroid label denotes an inferred location, not a measured point.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Require Identities, Geometry, And Frozen Location Sources"}

Require `s2_clinic_ids_df`, `s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf`, and
`s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf` from pages [20](20_page-construct-clinic-ids.qmd)
and [23](23_page-construct-healthsheds.qmd). Read the four exact source members
from the tracked `s2_clinic_months_raw_zip`; do not retrieve current master lists.
The GPS source describes FKT centers. Other location files mentioned only in
the legacy scratch section are not active inputs.

Reuse the page-23 spatial runtime and page-21 archive extraction helpers.
Spatial handoffs retain full field names, including `distance_csb_fkt` and
`fkt_instat_clean`, instead of reconstructing truncated shapefile names
`km_fkt` and `fkt_nst`. Raw source tables retain coordinate text and source IDs.
Scientific targets run only in the compute-node allocation. Rendering and
synthetic checks do not build targets.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Declare Source, Point, And Intersection Helpers"}

`unique_nonNA()` follows the legacy rule: remove missing values only when
nonmissing values exist, retaining multiple distinct values as ambiguity.
The unused legacy `mode()` has no consumer and is omitted.

Point conversion retains all original coordinate columns. Numeric coercion
has the legacy missing-coordinate behavior (`na.fail = FALSE`); malformed
text raises a coercion warning; the original text remains in the raw source
targets. No
coordinate swap, range clipping, or inferred sign correction is introduced.

The fields ending in `Contains` use `st_intersects()`, including boundary
intersections. The sparse result is checked at matching row indices, giving
the same diagonal as the legacy dense matrix without allocating that matrix.
An empty point produces `NA`, while a nonempty point against an empty polygon
produces zero. The input CRS and global s2 setting remain unchanged.

```{r}
s6_clinic_location_unique_nonNA_fn <- function(x) {
  x <- unique(x)
  if (any(is.na(x)) && !all(is.na(x))) x <- stats::na.omit(x)
  x
}
s6_clinic_location_read_fn <- function(archive, member) {
  s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn(archive, member, function(path) {
    read.csv(path, colClasses = "character", fileEncoding = "UTF-8",
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
}
s6_clinic_location_points_fn <- function(x) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  for (source in c("sect", "mdss", "who", "unicef", "gps")) {
    columns <- paste0(source, c("_x", "_y"))
    xy <- as.data.frame(lapply(x[columns], as.numeric))
    x[[paste0(source, "_ll")]] <- sf::st_geometry(sf::st_as_sf(
      xy, coords = columns, remove = FALSE, na.fail = FALSE, crs = 4326))
  }
  sf::st_as_sf(x, sf_column_name = "sect_ll")
}
s6_clinic_location_intersects_fn <- function(points, polygons) {
  stopifnot(length(points) == length(polygons))
  hits <- sf::st_intersects(points, polygons)
  result <- as.numeric(vapply(seq_along(hits), function(i) i %in% hits[[i]], logical(1)))
  result[sf::st_is_empty(points)] <- NA_real_
  result
}
s6_clinic_location_select_fn <- function(x) {
  mutate(x, which_use = case_when(
    who_ll_fktContains == 1 ~ "who",
    sect_ll_fktContains == 1 ~ "sect",
    unicef_ll_fktContains == 1 ~ "unicef",
    mdss_ll_fktContains == 1 ~ "mdss",
    gps_ll_shedContains == 1 ~ "gps",
    who_ll_shedContains == 1 ~ "who2",
    sect_ll_shedContains == 1 ~ "sect2",
    unicef_ll_shedContains == 1 ~ "unicef2",
    mdss_ll_shedContains == 1 ~ "mdss2",
    gps_ll_shedContains == 1 ~ "gps2",
    !sf::st_is_empty(fkt_geometry) ~ "fkt_centroid",
    !sf::st_is_empty(shed_geometry) ~ "shed_centroid",
    TRUE ~ "none"))
}
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Select Exact Archived Sources And Prepare Clinic Attributes"}

Only MDDSS's pair `(0, 0)` is excluded; an individual zero is not an exclusion
rule. The WHO longitude remains text until its reviewed trailing-minus repair.
Source rows with missing values retain the legacy filter behavior. All raw
text remains separately available for parsing diagnostics.

```{r}
s6_clinic_location_archive_members_chr <- {
  suffixes <- c(
    mdss = "data/raw/clinic_location_sources/MDDSS.csv",
    who = "data/raw/clinic_location_sources/WHO clinic master list.xlsx - SECTO DEPSI PUB.csv",
    unicef = "data/raw/clinic_location_sources/UNICEF clinic master list.xlsx - Feuil1.csv",
    gps = "data/raw/clinic_location_sources/CSB GPS points.txt")
  vapply(suffixes, function(suffix) s3_dictionary_archive_member_fn(
    s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, suffix), character(1))
}
s6_clinic_location_raw_sources_list <- lapply(s6_clinic_location_archive_members_chr,
  function(member) s6_clinic_location_read_fn(s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, member))
s6_clinic_location_mdss_source_df <- s6_clinic_location_raw_sources_list$mdss %>%
  mutate(across(c(Latitude, Longitude), as.numeric)) %>%
  filter(!(Latitude == 0 & Longitude == 0))
s6_clinic_location_other_sources_list <- list(
  who = s6_clinic_location_raw_sources_list$who %>%
    rename_with(function(x) gsub(".", "_", x, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(latitude = as.numeric(latitude)),
  unicef = s6_clinic_location_raw_sources_list$unicef,
  gps = s6_clinic_location_raw_sources_list$gps %>%
    mutate(across(c(Latitude, Longitude), as.numeric)))
s6_clinic_location_sectorization_df <- s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  summarise(across(c(region_uid:commune_name, fs_type, f_or_nf, fs_ll, fs_name),
                   s6_clinic_location_unique_nonNA_fn), .by = fs_uid) %>%
  mutate(public = grepl("CSB", fs_type), fs_ll_raw = fs_ll,
         fs_ll = gsub("POINT |\\(|\\)", "", fs_ll)) %>%
  tidyr::separate(fs_ll, into = c("sect_x", "sect_y"), sep = " ") %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("sect_"), ~as.numeric(na_if(.x, ""))))
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Join MDDSS Through Historical Clinic Codes"}

The first ranking chooses minimum cosine name distance within each FacilityID
across the historical crosswalk, after Latin-ASCII normalization. The second
ranking compares surviving MDDSS candidates with sectorization clinic names.
Equal minima survive; `min()` deliberately does not remove missing values.
The commented-out name threshold is not an active rule. Retain the identity
candidate table so unmatched codes and join expansion can be inspected.

```{r}
s6_clinic_location_mdss_identity_candidates_df <- s6_clinic_location_mdss_source_df %>%
  left_join(s2_clinic_ids_df %>%
    select(clinic_ID, cCodeStru, cNom) %>% distinct() %>%
    mutate(cCodeStru = as.character(cCodeStru),
           cNom = stringi::stri_trans_general(cNom, id = "Latin-ASCII")),
    by = c("FacilityID" = "cCodeStru"), multiple = "all") %>%
  mutate(name_dist = stringdist::stringdist(tolower(GeSISNom), tolower(cNom), method = "cosine"))
s6_clinic_location_mdss_joined_df <- {
  candidates <- s6_clinic_location_mdss_identity_candidates_df %>%
    filter(name_dist == min(name_dist), .by = FacilityID) %>%
    select(mdss_id = FacilityID, mdss_name = GeSISNom,
           mdss_x = Longitude, mdss_y = Latitude, clinic_ID) %>% distinct()
  s6_clinic_location_sectorization_df %>%
    left_join(candidates, by = c("fs_uid" = "clinic_ID")) %>%
    mutate(name_dist = stringdist::stringdist(tolower(mdss_name), tolower(fs_name), method = "cosine")) %>%
    filter(name_dist == min(name_dist) | n() == 1, .by = fs_uid) %>%
    select(-name_dist)
}
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Apply The Reviewed WHO Exceptions"}

UID replacements, four duplicate-name choices, five ambiguous UID exclusions,
and the `#N/A` exclusion follow legacy lines 143–173. The trailing ` -` in
**longitude** controls the sign of **latitude**. Keep that source-specific
repair literal; changing it would be a separate scientific correction.
The full join includes WHO-only clinics.

```{r}
s6_clinic_location_who_clean_df <- s6_clinic_location_other_sources_list$who %>%
  mutate(Facility_UID = case_when(grepl("SOATANANA", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "" ~ "VCf9Tra2OM4",
                                  grepl("MANGATANY", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "" ~ "GqEjMC845Qj",
                                  grepl("ZANAPOSA", Nom_complet_FS) ~ "Ba8QnbIIa3t",
                                  grepl("MANANDRIANA", Nom_complet_FS) ~ "yKbbKKhZicA",
                                  grepl("CARMMA ANDRAISORO", Nom_complet_FS) ~ "HmTrkNYWWOV",
                                  grepl("SERANAMBE", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A" ~ "YQ9XN4vE4T6",
                                  grepl("MAROVOVONANA", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A" ~ "xt1C9F1Flqu",
                                  grepl("ANTOKOBORITELO", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A" ~ "ealevALSs3e",
                                  grepl("INOSY", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A" ~ "KbA0FuyUEfY",
                                  grepl("MERIMANDROSO", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A" ~ "C4jmEurKKq2",
                                  grepl("ANJANOMANANA", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A"~ "GzJJVUSBpXW",
                                  grepl("ANTETEZANINTSINA", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A" ~ "LsevaLWVyXM",
                                  grepl("MANAKARA BE", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A" ~ "W5fydynAP1n",
                                  grepl("AMBODIAVIAVY", Nom_complet_FS) & Facility_UID == "#N/A" ~ "AxTFbOBjP1K",
                                  T ~ trimws(Facility_UID))) %>%
  select(fs_uid = Facility_UID, who_name = Nom_complet_FS, who_fkt = Nom_Fokontany_par_CSB,
         who_x = longitude, who_y = latitude) %>%
  filter(fs_uid != "#N/A") %>%
  # drop some incorrect entries (multiple rows for a single clinic, select the correct one)
  # or drop both if its unclear, or keep only the ll (not fkt) if same in both rows
  filter(fs_uid != "WmBYR1JepA7" | who_name == "CSB2 AMBODIMANGAVALO") %>%
  filter(fs_uid != "OGI9QrTBQy9" | who_name == "CSB2 AMPASY CSBU") %>%
  filter(fs_uid != "b912DLTCXvT" | who_name == "CSB2 MAROFANDILIA") %>%
  filter(fs_uid != "wLLSCFzaVc5" | who_name == "CSB2 BEREVO") %>%
  filter(fs_uid %in% c("p8ldnmLbC0v", "ZmPivRqpI9X", "hzPWgcl7y53",
                       "UgMnJXFhciB", "Og23D1GURi1") == FALSE) %>%
  # nrow # 2692
  group_by(fs_uid) %>%
  summarise(across(c(who_name, who_x, who_y), unique),
            who_fkt = case_when(n() == 1 ~ first(who_fkt))) %>% #nrow #2688
  mutate(who_y = ifelse(grepl(" -$", who_x), -who_y, who_y),
         who_x = gsub(" -$", "", who_x) %>% as.numeric)
s6_clinic_location_who_joined_df <- full_join(
  s6_clinic_location_mdss_joined_df, s6_clinic_location_who_clean_df, by = "fs_uid")
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Add UNICEF And GPS Candidates"}

UNICEF's bracketed pair is longitude then latitude. GPS points join historical
GESIS codes, preserve closest-name ties, and exclude the code `110443043`
and the name `AMBALABONGO` independently. The GPS full join uses all shared
columns, as in the legacy call; its candidate table exposes those columns.

```{r}
s6_clinic_location_unicef_joined_df <- full_join(
  s6_clinic_location_who_joined_df,
  s6_clinic_location_other_sources_list$unicef %>%
    mutate(Coordinates_raw = Coordinates, Coordinates = gsub("\\[|\\]", "", Coordinates)) %>%
    tidyr::separate(Coordinates, c("unicef_x", "unicef_y"), sep = ",") %>%
    rename(unicef_name = Name, fs_uid = UID, unicef_commune_uid = Parent.UID),
  by = "fs_uid")
s6_clinic_location_gps_identity_candidates_df <- s6_clinic_location_other_sources_list$gps %>%
  filter(clinic_cod != "110443043" & clinic_nam != "AMBALABONGO") %>%
  left_join(s2_clinic_ids_df %>%
    select(clinic_ID, cCodeStru, cNom) %>% distinct() %>%
    mutate(cCodeStru = as.character(cCodeStru),
           cNom = stringi::stri_trans_general(cNom, id = "Latin-ASCII")),
    by = c("clinic_cod" = "cCodeStru"), multiple = "all") %>%
  mutate(name_dist = stringdist::stringdist(tolower(clinic_nam), tolower(cNom), method = "cosine"))
s6_clinic_location_gps_joined_df <- full_join(
  s6_clinic_location_unicef_joined_df,
  s6_clinic_location_gps_identity_candidates_df %>%
    filter(name_dist == min(name_dist), .by = clinic_cod) %>%
    select(gps_gesis = clinic_cod, gps_name = clinic_nam,
           gps_x = Longitude, gps_y = Latitude, fs_uid = clinic_ID) %>% distinct(),
  multiple = "all")
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Identify A Unique Matching FKT"}

Keep the combined minimum-name-distance, `<= 0.12` or name-containment, and
minimum-geographic-distance condition. A single FKT qualifies independently
of that condition. Distances retain the legacy comma and kilometer-string
conversion. `sum()` and name `min()` retain missing values; ties or missing
evidence may prevent a unique match rather than force a winner. The full
ranked table remains available, including rejected candidates.

Name containment uses stringi's ICU regex matcher, the same regex engine
used by stringr, with missing patterns propagated as `NA`. A missing clinic
name becomes the pattern in the reverse containment test; stringr rejects
that pattern before matching. Retaining `NA` preserves unknown evidence and
the separate single-FKT rule without dropping assignment rows or filling
missing names with empty strings.

```{r}
s6_clinic_location_fkt_candidates_fn <- function(sect) {
  sect %>% filter(fkt_name != "" & !is.na(fkt_name)) %>%
    mutate(name_noPre = gsub("CSB1 |CSB2 |HP_|HP |FSP_|FSP_ |FSP ", "", fs_name),
      fkt_fs_stringdist = stringdist::stringdist(tolower(name_noPre), tolower(fkt_name), method = "cosine"),
      name_contain = stringi::stri_detect_regex(tolower(name_noPre), tolower(fkt_name)) |
        stringi::stri_detect_regex(tolower(fkt_name), tolower(name_noPre)),
      dist = gsub(",", ".", distance_csb_fkt) %>%
        gsub("Km|Km| km|km", "", .) %>% na_if("") %>% as.numeric()) %>%
    group_by(fs_uid) %>%
    mutate(n_fkt = n(),
      match_name_dist = (fkt_fs_stringdist == min(fkt_fs_stringdist) &
        (fkt_fs_stringdist <= 0.12 | name_contain) & dist == min(dist, na.rm = TRUE)) | n_fkt == 1,
      n_match = sum(match_name_dist)) %>% ungroup()
}
s6_clinic_location_fkt_candidates_sf <- s6_clinic_location_fkt_candidates_fn(s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf)
s6_clinic_location_fkt_matched_df <- full_join(
  s6_clinic_location_gps_joined_df,
  s6_clinic_location_fkt_candidates_sf %>%
    filter(n_match == 1 & match_name_dist) %>%
    select(fs_uid, fkt_uid, fkt_name, fkt_instat_clean, fkt_geometry = geometry,
           fkt_fs_stringdist, fkt_fs_geodist = dist) %>% as.data.frame(),
  by = "fs_uid")
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Calculate Spatial Evidence And Select The Preferred Source"}

The selected target retains all five point columns, raw coordinates, FKT and
healthshed geometries, intersection evidence, and `which_use`. Its active
geometry is `sect_ll`; that column is a candidate, not the selected point.
Page 25 must extract the point identified by `which_use` or compute the stated
centroid. A location selected from GPS still represents the source's FKT center.

| Priority | Evidence | Label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–4 | WHO, sectorization, UNICEF, MDDSS intersects the matched FKT | `who`, `sect`, `unicef`, `mdss` |
| 5 | GPS intersects the healthshed | `gps` |
| 6–10 | WHO, sectorization, UNICEF, MDDSS, GPS intersects the healthshed | `who2`, `sect2`, `unicef2`, `mdss2`, `gps2` |
| 11–13 | Nonempty FKT, nonempty healthshed, neither | `fkt_centroid`, `shed_centroid`, `none` |

The second GPS predicate is redundant in the legacy first-match order;
`gps2` is retained in code and need not occur. This page selects source labels
without implementing page 25's coordinate extraction. The legacy metadata
script omits UNICEF extraction. Page 25 records the reviewed decision to
preserve those missing coordinates for legacy parity. Do not change selection
here to hide that gap.

```{r}
s6_clinic_location_points_sf <- {
  s5_spatial_runtime_list
  s6_clinic_location_points_fn(s6_clinic_location_fkt_matched_df)
}
s6_clinic_location_containment_sf <- {
  x <- left_join(s6_clinic_location_points_sf,
    as.data.frame(select(s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf, fs_uid, shed_geometry = geometry)),
    by = "fs_uid")
  for (source in c("sect", "mdss", "who", "unicef", "gps")) {
    column <- paste0(source, "_ll")
    x[[column]] <- sf::st_set_crs(x[[column]], 4326)
    x[[paste0(column, "_fktContains")]] <- s6_clinic_location_intersects_fn(x[[column]], x$fkt_geometry)
    x[[paste0(column, "_shedContains")]] <- s6_clinic_location_intersects_fn(x[[column]], x$shed_geometry)
  }
  x
}
s6_clinic_locations_selected_sf <- s6_clinic_location_select_fn(s6_clinic_location_containment_sf)
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Retain Parsing, Multiplicity, And Intersection Audits"}

Audit tables count candidate **rows**, not unique clinics. Denominators for
intersection fractions exclude missing points, matching the legacy diagnostic.
Multiple candidates are evidence to inspect, not a condition repaired by
`distinct(fs_uid, .keep_all = TRUE)`. Audits stay in ordinary targets; the full
spatial evidence remains the page-25 handoff. The parsing audit describes
values that reach point conversion; inspect the raw source tables and
`fs_ll_raw` for text coerced during earlier source preparation.

```{r}
s6_clinic_location_parse_audit_df <- {
  x <- sf::st_drop_geometry(s6_clinic_locations_selected_sf)
  bind_rows(lapply(c("sect", "mdss", "who", "unicef", "gps"), function(source) {
    raw_x <- x[[paste0(source, "_x")]]
    raw_y <- x[[paste0(source, "_y")]]
    num_x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(raw_x))
    num_y <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(raw_y))
    tibble::tibble(fs_uid = x$fs_uid, source = source,
      raw_x = as.character(raw_x), raw_y = as.character(raw_y), x = num_x, y = num_y,
      missing_pair = is.na(num_x) | is.na(num_y),
      invalid_x = !is.na(raw_x) & trimws(as.character(raw_x)) != "" & is.na(num_x),
      invalid_y = !is.na(raw_y) & trimws(as.character(raw_y)) != "" & is.na(num_y))
  }))
}
s6_clinic_location_multiplicity_audit_df <- {
  stages <- list(sectorization = s6_clinic_location_sectorization_df,
    mdss = s6_clinic_location_mdss_joined_df, who = s6_clinic_location_who_joined_df,
    unicef = s6_clinic_location_unicef_joined_df, gps = s6_clinic_location_gps_joined_df,
    selected = s6_clinic_locations_selected_sf)
  bind_rows(lapply(names(stages), function(stage) {
    x <- s5_healthshed_drop_geometry_fn(stages[[stage]])
    count(x, fs_uid, name = "candidate_rows") %>% mutate(stage = stage)
  }))
}
s6_clinic_location_intersection_audit_df <- {
  x <- s6_clinic_locations_selected_sf
  bind_rows(lapply(c("sect", "mdss", "who", "unicef", "gps"), function(source) {
    bind_rows(lapply(c("fkt", "shed"), function(polygon) {
      values <- x[[paste0(source, "_ll_", polygon, "Contains")]]
      tibble::tibble(source = source, polygon = polygon, rows = length(values),
        n = sum(!is.na(values)), success = sum(values, na.rm = TRUE),
        fraction = sum(values, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(!is.na(values)))
    }))
  }))
}
```

::: {.manual-check title="Inspect Location Evidence Against The Most Recent Archived Data"}

Run static graph validation and synthetic fixtures without building scientific
targets. The fixture suite tests parsing, corrections, ties, row-aligned spatial
predicates, and the source-selection order.

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript tests/check-clinic-location-rules.R
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript tests/check-data-storage-convention.R
python3 tests/check-manual-structure.py
```

After running S6 on the compute node, use the following **interactive,
read-only EDA prompts**. These are plain R examples, not tangled target
declarations or render-time computation. They read the built target store and
the selected most recent archived data; no output is written and no target is built.
The [baseline selection](mapping/legacy-pipeline-map.qmd#most-recent-archived-data-comparison-baseline)
uses the October 2024 ZIP clinic-location output, the latest iteration found
for this stage. Keep research
records and maps in the authorized analysis session, outside public HTML.

**Current scope (2026-11-08).** Shape checks are sufficient for this development
step; the researcher reports that the initial checks on pages 18–21 appear
to pass. Start with dimensions, column layout, and source-selection counts
below. The subsequent EDA remains available for investigating discrepancies;
passing shape checks does not establish coordinate equality.

**Are the most recent archived data and current pipeline clinic populations comparable?** First compare clinic
sets and multiplicity. Do not pair ambiguous rows by arbitrary row order.

```r
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(sf)
new <- targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_locations_selected_sf)
archived_baseline <- dget(here::here("src", "archived-comparison-baseline.R"))
archive <- here::here(archived_baseline$archive_zip)
member <- archived_baseline$clinic_locations_member
old <- targets::tar_read(s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn)(archive, member, readRDS)
plain <- function(x) as.data.frame(x)[!vapply(as.data.frame(x), inherits, logical(1), what = "sfc")]
old_rows <- plain(old)
new_rows <- plain(new)
```

**Rows, nonspatial columns, and UID multiplicity side by side.** All `sfc`
columns are excluded by `plain()`; this is an attribute-table schema check.
`extra_uid_rows` counts rows beyond one per distinct UID, including missing
UID as a group. Review missing IDs and multiplicity separately.

```r
# Shape check: locations-dimensions
location_shape <- function(x) tibble::tibble(
  rows = nrow(x), columns = length(names(x)),
  clinics = dplyr::n_distinct(x$fs_uid, na.rm = TRUE),
  missing_uids = sum(is.na(x$fs_uid) | x$fs_uid == ""),
  extra_uid_rows = nrow(x) - dplyr::n_distinct(x$fs_uid)
)
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = location_shape(old_rows),
  `current pipeline` = location_shape(new_rows), .id = "source"
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-source, names_to = "metric", values_to = "count") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = count) |>
  dplyr::mutate(difference = `current pipeline` - `most recent archived data`) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```r
# Shape check: locations-schema
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = tibble::tibble(position = seq_along(names(old_rows)), column = names(old_rows)),
  `current pipeline` = tibble::tibble(position = seq_along(names(new_rows)), column = names(new_rows)),
  .id = "source"
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = column) |>
  dplyr::arrange(position) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

**Source-selection counts.** Absent categories contribute zero rows;
`difference` is current minus archived. These are candidate-row counts,
not counts of uniquely located clinics.

```r
# Shape check: locations-sources
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = dplyr::count(old_rows, which_use, name = "rows"),
  `current pipeline` = dplyr::count(new_rows, which_use, name = "rows"),
  .id = "source"
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = rows, values_fill = 0L) |>
  dplyr::mutate(difference = `current pipeline` - `most recent archived data`) |>
  dplyr::arrange(which_use) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

Continue to clinic-set and saved multiplicity evidence when needed:

```r
anti_join(distinct(old_rows, fs_uid), distinct(new_rows, fs_uid), by = "fs_uid")
anti_join(distinct(new_rows, fs_uid), distinct(old_rows, fs_uid), by = "fs_uid")
targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_location_multiplicity_audit_df) %>% filter(candidate_rows > 1 | is.na(fs_uid))
```

**Which selection decisions changed, and is the change upstream of S6?**
Restrict the first paired comparison to UIDs with exactly one row in each
output, including equal missing labels. Compare the candidate coordinates and
intersection evidence before attributing a difference to source precedence.
S5 geometry differences and native-library changes may also explain it.

```r
unique_old <- old_rows %>% filter(n() == 1 & !is.na(fs_uid), .by = fs_uid)
unique_new <- new_rows %>% filter(n() == 1 & !is.na(fs_uid), .by = fs_uid)
paired <- inner_join(unique_old, unique_new, by = "fs_uid", suffix = c("_old", "_new"))
paired %>% count(which_use_old, which_use_new, sort = TRUE)
changed <- paired %>% filter(!(coalesce(which_use_old == which_use_new, FALSE) |
  (is.na(which_use_old) & is.na(which_use_new))))
changed %>% select(fs_uid, starts_with("which_use"), matches("_(x|y)_(old|new)$"))
# For an individual changed UID, inspect the evidence and source records:
# new[new$fs_uid == changed$fs_uid[[1]], ]
# targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_location_fkt_candidates_sf) %>% filter(fs_uid == changed$fs_uid[[1]])
```

**Are source points identical, merely rounded, or genuinely different?**
Use WGS84 point distances in meters on the uniquely paired UIDs. Keep missing
pairs separate and inspect large differences by UID. This compares source
candidates, not final coordinates or centroid accuracy.

```r
candidate_distance <- bind_rows(lapply(c("sect", "mdss", "who", "unicef", "gps"), function(source) {
  a <- old[[paste0(source, "_ll")]][match(paired$fs_uid, old$fs_uid)]
  b <- new[[paste0(source, "_ll")]][match(paired$fs_uid, new$fs_uid)]
  tibble(fs_uid = paired$fs_uid, source = source,
    old_empty = st_is_empty(a), new_empty = st_is_empty(b),
    meters = as.numeric(st_distance(a, b, by_element = TRUE)))
}))
candidate_distance %>% summarise(rows = n(), missing = sum(is.na(meters)),
  maximum_m = if (all(is.na(meters))) NA_real_ else max(meters, na.rm = TRUE), .by = source)
candidate_distance %>% filter(!is.na(meters)) %>% arrange(desc(meters)) %>% head(20)
```

**What is the denominator behind each apparent success rate?** Compare
row-level intersection summaries, then inspect malformed coordinates,
unmatched historical codes, and FKT ambiguities. A high fraction is not proof
of individual coordinate accuracy. The old output omits `shed_geometry`, so
geometry-level diagnosis also needs the frozen old healthsheds and S5 audit.

```r
targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_location_intersection_audit_df)
old_intersections <- bind_rows(lapply(grep("Contains$", names(old_rows), value = TRUE), function(column) {
  values <- old_rows[[column]]
  tibble(column = column, n = sum(!is.na(values)), success = sum(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    fraction = sum(values, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(!is.na(values)))
}))
old_intersections
targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_location_parse_audit_df) %>% filter(invalid_x | invalid_y | missing_pair)
targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_location_mdss_identity_candidates_df) %>% filter(is.na(clinic_ID))
targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_location_gps_identity_candidates_df) %>% filter(is.na(clinic_ID))
targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_location_fkt_candidates_sf) %>% filter(is.na(n_match) | n_match > 1)
```

**Which missing values precede name matching or point conversion?** A missing
clinic name is unknown name-match evidence. Missing pieces and numeric
coercion warnings in sectorization coordinates are separate diagnostics;
inspect their original WKT before proposing a parsing correction.

```r
targets::tar_read(s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf) %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(is.na(fs_name)) %>% count(match_type, sort = TRUE)
targets::tar_read(s6_clinic_location_sectorization_df) %>%
  filter(is.na(sect_x) | is.na(sect_y)) %>% count(fs_ll_raw, sort = TRUE)
```

Full-data parity remains to be evaluated on the compute node. Page 25 records
the UNICEF extraction policy as explicit legacy missing-coordinate parity. Historical counts are observations, not fixed assertions.
